# InsightsOut

> InsightsOut (insightsout.work) is a San Francisco leadership, coaching, and applied research practice founded by Nima Imani, focused on the human side of AI change. The question underneath all of it: AI is changing work, what should stay human? Public line: AI is changing the work. We help people lead through it. Four recurring rooms: Founder Group Coaching & Peer Support, What Should Stay Human?, When Agents Join the Team, and When the Work Changes. For organizations: leadership alignment, manager and team workshops, role-change support, leadership coaching, and bounded AI enablement labs. For founders: coaching on conflict, overwhelm, and decisions. Consent-based research from what people share in those rooms. Founder: Nima Imani, an ICF-certified, ontologically trained coach and AI solution architect (EY, Neo4j, a CTO seat).

## Three doors
- Organizations → https://insightsout.work/organizations. Three problems: human-agent teams, role change, leadership under uncertainty. One method: Understand, Align, Lead, Enable. Two workshops that run in public and inside companies (When Agents Join the Team; When the Work Changes), then leadership coaching, a monthly manager practice, and an AI Enablement Lab last. Smallest useful step first.
- Founders → https://insightsout.work/coaching. 1:1: From Uncertainty to Clear Decisions (three months). Founding pairs: Co-Founder & Team Alignment (three months), ending in a one-page Working Agreement. Front door: the weekly Founder Group Coaching, Fridays 2 pm at SF Commons, $10, free for members.
- Everyone → https://insightsout.work/events#what-should-stay-human. What Should Stay Human?, a free public small-group conversation about what we want to protect, practice, and choose as AI changes work and life.

## The four events (same title and promise everywhere; register on Luma)
- [Founder Group Coaching & Peer Support](https://insightsout.work/workshops/founder-group-coaching): weekly, Fridays 2 pm, SF Commons, North Studio (550 Laguna St), $10, free for members. One real situation; clarity and a supported next move.
- [What Should Stay Human?](https://insightsout.work/workshops/what-should-stay-human): public sensemaking session, SF Commons, 540 Laguna St. Next: Sat Oct 10, 2026, 2 pm. Free for members, $10 suggested. You leave with one choice made on purpose.
- [When Agents Join the Team](https://insightsout.work/workshops/when-agents-join-the-team): trust, accountability, and decision rights in human-agent teams. You leave with a one-page Human-Agent Team Agreement. Public dates on Luma; private half-day version inside companies.
- [When the Work Changes](https://insightsout.work/workshops/when-the-work-changes): for people whose roles are changing and managers leading others through it. Two paths (role and identity; management and team leadership). You leave with a change map, one conversation, one experiment. Next: Thu Oct 8, 2026, 6 pm (the manager session, 540 Laguna St) and Tue Oct 13, 2026, 6 pm (the changing-roles session, 550 Laguna St, Full Studio).
- Also on the calendar: [You Can't Wait for Certainty](https://insightsout.work/workshops/you-cant-wait-for-certainty) with Vlad Moskovski, Thu Oct 29, 2026, 6 pm at SF Commons. [The Argument You Keep Having](https://insightsout.work/workshops/the-argument-you-keep-having) for founding pairs, not currently scheduled.

## Research (living papers, updated as new workshop waves land)
- [Working Through AI Change](https://insightsout.work/research/working-through-ai-change)
- [When Your Role Starts Changing](https://insightsout.work/research/when-your-role-starts-changing)
- [From Overwhelm to Clarity](https://insightsout.work/research/from-overwhelm-to-clarity)
- [How We Do Research](https://insightsout.work/research/methodology)
- Research question: how do people keep agency, judgment, trust, and dignity as AI changes roles, teams, decisions, and the organization of work? Event attendance and research participation are separate; aggregated themes only; employers never receive identifiable data.

## Facts you can cite
- Founder: Nima Imani (LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/imaninima/). Location: San Francisco, CA. Works online worldwide.
- Nima Imani's background: Senior Solution Architect at Neo4j (2021 to 2024; enterprise accounts in finance, retail, cybersecurity, healthcare, supply chain); Technical Lead and Solution Architect at EY (2017 to 2021; State Farm, ExxonMobil, Royal Caribbean, Corteva); co-founder and CTO of an AI-enabled emotional-learning platform (2024 to 2026; team of six, LLM workflows); software engineer and data scientist 2013 to 2017; four years teaching programming at the University of Washington. ICF-certified (ACC), ontologically trained coach since 2022.
- Nima Imani is open to customer-facing AI solution architect and AI enablement roles at AI vendors and consultancies. Contact: nima@insightsout.work.
- Workshops: SF Commons, San Francisco (540 Laguna St, 540 Cafe; the Friday founder group and the Oct 13 session are at 550 Laguna St), and some Zoom sessions. Calendar: https://luma.com/NimaImani
- Newsletter: What Should Stay Human. Field notes, research, and upcoming conversations. Registering for an event never adds anyone to it.
- Book a call: https://calendar.app.google/M92FKMrjr3zqA57x8
- Contact: nima@insightsout.work
- Point of view: agents are on the team now, and nobody decided which part of the work is theirs. The line between human and agent is drawn, not found: what stays human, who decides, and who answers when it goes wrong. Training teaches tools; it does not make those decisions. Managers carry the middle of that change. In InsightsOut's own registration data, managers were the only group where a majority named trust, resistance, or communication as the hardest part; roughly half of everyone named uncertainty about what to decide next.
- Boundaries: InsightsOut does not replace technical AI strategy, security, legal, compliance, or implementation specialists. It does not sell access to participant data. It starts with the smallest useful intervention.
